chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskhan from Muhammad al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who buys fruit, then sells it before he takes possession of it. He said: 'There is no harm in it; if he finds profit, let him sell it.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell fruit before taking possession in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that selling fruit before physical possession is permissible if the seller finds profit, reflecting the Shia juristic preference for flexibility in agricultural trade to avoid hardship. This ruling aligns with the principle of *qabd* (possession) being interpreted as effective rather than strictly physical in certain commercial contexts, distinguishing it from stricter Hanafi or Maliki views on *bay' al-mu'awwadah*. The hadith underscores the practical economic considerations in early Islamic markets, where perishable goods required swift transaction mechanisms.
